findings.title: should_block? has write side effects on every validation and is not atomic
findings.body: should_block? increments match_count and saves the record each time it is called, and it is invoked from the EmailValidator on every validation of the email attribute. Read-only checks therefore perform UPDATEs, and the non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count (record.match_count += 1 then save) loses increments under concurrent signups. Use an atomic update_all/increment or move the statistics update out of the predicate.

findings.title: Email lookup is case sensitive while emails are normalized elsewhere
findings.body: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) does an exact match, but the rest of the code downcases emails (Email.downcase in change_email and find_by_username_or_email). A blocked address stored as lowercase will not block 'Bad@Spam.com', letting the blocked user bypass the block trivially.

findings.title: Blocked-email check runs against nil or non-string values
findings.body: validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) without guarding against a nil or blank value; the email attribute can be nil if presence validation fails, and the domain check also assumes a string. This can cause a query with nil or an error in the validator chain.

findings.title: Blocked-email check only runs when email changed, and the uniqueness check is now bypassed for validator order
findings.body: The email validator is now declared with if: :email_changed?, and the blocklist check is added inside the validator. Existing users whose addresses are later added to the blocklist are never re-checked, and the presence/uniqueness validations moved to a single line, changing error ordering. Confirm the intended behaviour for already-registered users.

findings.title: Create response leaks submitted values and error details to the client
findings.body: The failure response now returns user.errors.to_hash and user.attributes.slice(...) which includes the submitted email. Combined with the blocklist, this lets a client probe the blocklist by seeing which errors are returned, and the change is unrelated to the stated purpose. The error payload should be limited to what the client needs.

findings.title: rejectedEmails stores server-supplied email and never clears it
findings.body: The rejectedEmails array is populated from result.values.email whenever the server reports an email error, and entries are never removed. If the user corrects the email to something else, the validation still uses contains() on the list, and a blocked email that the server rejected is rejected client-side permanently for the session. Also, the array is shared on the prototype via Em.A, which is a per-controller-instance concern only if constructed per instance.

findings.title: action_type column has no default, and the model has no DB-level guard for it
findings.body: action_type is null: false with no default; the default is supplied only by a before_validation callback. Inserts that bypass validation (update_all, raw SQL, or fixtures) will fail or the enum will be invalid. Consider a DB default.

findings.title: Validator spec does not cover whitelist/blacklist behaviour or unchanged blocked-email path
findings.body: The spec only stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? and never exercises the whitelist/blacklist branches it was moved from, nor the case where a non-string or nil value is passed. Tests of the moved logic were removed from the User spec without equivalent coverage here.
